p.src: The local god said, “The Great King of Mighty Strength is none other than the Bull Demon King.” Pilgrim said, “So this mountain was set ablaze by the Bull Demon King and is merely called the Mountain of Flames?” The local god said, “No, no. Only if the Great Sage will pardon my offense shall I dare speak frankly.” Pilgrim said, “What offense have you committed? Speak freely.” The local god said, “This fire was originally started by you, Great Sage.” Pilgrim said angrily, “Where was I then? What nonsense you speak! Am I the sort to go about setting fires?” The local god said, “So you no longer recognize me. Originally there was no mountain here. Five hundred years ago, when you caused havoc in Heaven, the Illustrious Sage captured you and delivered you to Lord Lao, who placed you inside the Eight-Trigram Furnace. After the firing, when the furnace was opened, you kicked it over. Several bricks fell from it, still holding embers, and when they landed here they became the Mountain of Flames. I was once the Daoist charged with tending the furnace in the Tushita Palace. Lord Lao blamed me for failing in my duty and banished me here, where I became the local god of the Mountain of Flames.” Hearing this, Zhu Bajie said resentfully, “No wonder you are dressed like that. So you are a local god who used to be a Daoist.”

p.src: Still only half convinced, Pilgrim said, “Then tell me why you wanted me to seek the Great King of Mighty Strength earlier.” The local god said, “The Great King of Mighty Strength is the Rakshasa Woman’s husband. Lately he has abandoned the Rakshasa Woman and now lives in the Cloud-Touching Cave on Mount Accumulated Thunder. There was a Fox King of Ten Thousand Years who died and left behind a daughter named Princess Jade Countenance. The princess possessed a fortune worth millions, but had no one to manage it. Two years ago, hearing of the Bull Demon King’s immense powers, she willingly offered her fortune as a dowry and took him into her household as her husband. The Bull King abandoned the Rakshasa Woman and has not looked back for a long time. If the Great Sage finds the Bull King and implores him to come here, only then will you be able to borrow the true fan: first, it will fan out the flames and allow your master to continue his journey; second, it will end the danger of fire forever and protect every living creature in this land; and third, it will release me to return to Heaven and report the fulfillment of Lord Lao’s decree.” Pilgrim said, “Where is Mount Accumulated Thunder? How far is it from here?” The local god said, “It lies due south. It is more than three thousand li from here.”

p.src: As the woman gradually approached the rock, the Great Sage bowed and asked gently, “Where are you going, gracious lady?” The woman had not noticed him, but on hearing the question, she raised her head. Suddenly seeing the Great Sage’s ugly features, she was terribly frightened. Unable either to retreat or go forward, she could only answer with trembling reluctance, “Where have you come from? How dare you question anyone here?” The Great Sage thought, “If I tell her about the quest for the scriptures and my need for the fan, I fear this creature may be related to the Bull King. I had better pretend to be acting on behalf of a kinswoman and say that I have come to invite the Demon King.” Seeing him remain silent, the woman’s expression changed, and she shouted angrily, “Who are you, to dare come and question me?” The Great Sage bowed and said with an apologetic smile, “I come from Mount Green Cloud and have only just arrived in your honored region, so I do not know the way. May I ask, gracious lady, whether this is Mount Accumulated Thunder?” The woman said, “It is.” The Great Sage said, “Where is the Cloud-Touching Cave?” The woman said, “What business have you with that cave?” The Great Sage said, “Princess Iron Fan of Plantain Cave on Mount Green Cloud sent me to invite the Bull Demon King.”

p.src: When the woman heard that Princess Iron Fan was inviting the Bull Demon King, she flew into a rage, turning red to the very roots of her ears, and cursed shrilly, “That worthless slut is truly shameless and ignorant! The Bull King has been in my household less than two years, yet who knows how many pearls, jewels, gold and silver, silks and satins I have given him? I provide his firewood every year and his rice every month, so he lives here in perfect ease. Still she has no shame and sends for him again—what does she want with him?” At these words the Great Sage knew that she was Princess Jade Countenance. Deliberately drawing his gold-banded cudgel, he roared, “You vicious wench! You used your fortune to buy the Bull King’s devotion, truly paying money to acquire a husband. You ought to be ashamed yourself—how dare you abuse anyone else?” When the woman saw it, terror scattered her wits and soul. Losing all composure, she stumbled wildly on her little bound feet and turned to flee, trembling all over. The Great Sage followed close behind, shouting and bellowing. Beyond the pine shade, as it happened, lay the entrance to the Cloud-Touching Cave. The woman ran inside and slammed the gate shut. The Great Sage put away his gold-banded cudgel, halted, and looked around. What a splendid place it was:

p.src: We shall say no more for now of Pilgrim admiring the scenery. We tell instead how the woman, her powdered face streaming with sweat and her delicate heart still pounding with fright, ran straight into the study. The Bull Demon King happened to be there, quietly studying an alchemical text. In a furious state, the woman collapsed into his arms, clawed at her ears and cheeks, and burst into loud sobs. The Bull King smiled ingratiatingly and said, “My beauty, do not be upset. Tell me what has happened.” The woman stamped and thrashed about, crying, “You wretched demon, you have brought about my death!” The Bull King laughed and said, “Why are you cursing me?” The woman said, “With neither father nor mother to depend upon, I took you as my husband so that you would protect me and preserve my life. People throughout the realm call you a fine hero, but you are nothing more than a useless coward afraid of his wife.” Hearing this, the Bull King embraced her and said, “My beauty, what have I done wrong? Tell me slowly, and I shall apologize to you.” The woman said, “Just now I was strolling among the flowers outside the cave, gathering orchids and fragrant herbs, when a monk with a hairy face and a thunder-god’s beak suddenly came up and bowed to me, frightening me senseless. When I recovered and asked who he was, he said that Princess Iron Fan had sent him to invite the Bull Demon King. I said a couple of things to him, but he cursed me at length and chased me with a cudgel to beat me. Had I not run quickly, he would almost certainly have beaten me to death. Have I not invited calamity by taking you in? You have brought about my death!” On hearing this, the Bull King composed his expression and apologized to her. He soothed her tenderly for a long while before her anger finally subsided. Then the Demon King said fiercely, “My beauty, I would not dare conceal the truth from you. Though Plantain Cave lies in a remote and quiet place, it is secluded, serene, and carefree. My wife has practiced self-cultivation since childhood and is an immortal maiden who has attained the Way. Moreover, her household is strictly ordered and contains not even a young male servant. How could she possibly have sent a man with a thunder-god’s beak? This must be some demon from elsewhere, perhaps using her name as a pretext to come looking for me. Wait here while I go out and see.”

p.src: The Great Sage straightened his clothes, stepped forward, and bowed deeply. “Elder Brother, do you still recognize your little brother?” The Bull King returned his salute. “Are you Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven?” The Great Sage said, “Indeed I am, indeed I am. We have long been parted, and I have not had the chance to pay my respects. I came here just now and questioned a woman, and only then was able to see you. Your noble bearing is finer than ever—truly a cause for celebration.” The Bull King shouted, “Enough of your glib tongue! I heard that after you wreaked havoc in Heaven, the Buddha subdued you beneath Five Elements Mountain. Recently freed from that divine punishment, you began escorting the Tang monk westward to see the Buddha and seek the scriptures. Why, then, did you harm my young son, Bull Sage Infant, in Fire-Cloud Cave at Withered-Pine Ravine on Mount Hao? I was just here nursing my anger against you, yet you dare come looking for me again?” The Great Sage bowed and said, “Elder Brother, please do not blame your little brother unjustly. At the time, your honored son seized my master and meant to eat his flesh. I could not get near him, but fortunately the Bodhisattva Guanyin, wishing to save my master, persuaded him to return to the righteous path. He is now the Boy of Sudhana, ranked even higher than you. He enjoys the portals and halls of supreme bliss and possesses everlasting freedom and longevity. What could be wrong with that, and why blame me instead?” The Bull King cursed him. “You smooth-tongued macaque! You have talked your way past the matter of harming my son; but why did you just now insult my beloved concubine and beat your way to my door?” The Great Sage laughed. “I came to pay my respects to you, Elder Brother, but could not find you, so I questioned that woman. I did not know she was my second sister-in-law. She cursed me a few times, and in a moment of roughness I startled her. I beg you to forgive me, Elder Brother.” The Bull King said, “If that is how it was, then for the sake of our old friendship I shall spare you. Be gone.”

p.src: The Great Sage said, “I am endlessly grateful for your generous pardon. There is still one matter on which I must trouble you, and I earnestly hope you will assist me.” The Bull King cursed him. “This macaque has no sense of propriety! I spare you, yet instead of leaving, you stay to pester me. What assistance do you want?” The Great Sage said, “To tell you the truth, Elder Brother, I am escorting the Tang monk westward, but our road is blocked by the Mountain of Flames and we cannot proceed. I asked the local people and learned that your honored wife, Princess Rakshasi, possesses a Plantain Fan, which I wished to borrow for a time. Yesterday I went to your former residence to pay my respects to my sister-in-law, but she resolutely refused to lend it. That is why I have come especially to ask you, Elder Brother. I beg you to show boundless compassion and accompany me to your first wife's residence. Please, by all means, have her lend me the fan so that I may fan out the flames and escort the Tang monk across the mountain. I shall return it intact at once.” At these words, the Bull King's heart blazed with fury. Grinding his steel-hard teeth, he cursed, “You claim you have committed no offense, but now I see it was all because you wanted the fan! You must first have insulted my wife; when she refused you, you came looking for me and then even drove off my beloved concubine. As the saying goes, ‘A friend's wife must never be dishonored; a friend's concubine must never be harmed.’ You have both dishonored my wife and harmed my concubine—how grossly discourteous can you be? Come and take a blow from my cudgel!” The Great Sage said, “If you want to fight, Brother, I am not afraid. But I sincerely seek the treasure, and I beg you to let me borrow it for a while.” The Bull King said, “If you can withstand me for three rounds, I shall have my wife lend it to you; but if you cannot, I shall beat you to death and avenge myself.” The Great Sage said, “That is fair, Brother. I have been rather idle of late and have not met with you. I do not know how your martial skill has changed over these past years, so let us brothers display our cudgel craft.” The Bull King would hear no more. He drew his wrought-iron cudgel and struck straight at the Great Sage's head; the Great Sage raised his golden-hooped staff and met the blow at once. A splendid battle followed between the two:

p.src: The Great Sage and the Bull King fought for well over a hundred rounds without either gaining the advantage. Just as they were locked in an inextricable struggle, someone called from the mountain peak, “Grand Lord Bull, my king sends you his most respectful greetings and begs you to come at once, so that you may take your honored seat.” Hearing this, the Bull King braced his wrought-iron cudgel against the golden-hooped staff and called, “Macaque, stop for now and wait while I attend a gathering at a friend's house.” With that, he lowered his cloud and went straight into the cave. He said to Princess Jade Countenance, “My beauty, that thunder-god-mouthed fellow just now was the macaque Sun Wukong. I gave him such a cudgeling that he fled and will never dare return. Set your mind at ease and enjoy yourself. I am going to drink at a friend's place.” He took off his armor, put on a dark blue cropped-velvet jacket, went out, and mounted the Golden-Eyed Beast that Parts the Waters. After ordering his underlings to guard the gate, he traveled half in cloud and half in mist straight toward the northwest.

p.src: Watching from the high peak, the Great Sage thought to himself, “I wonder what other friend this old bull has made and where he is going to attend a gathering. Let old Sun follow him and see.” What a resourceful Pilgrim! He shook himself, changed into a gust of fresh wind, caught up with the Bull King, and followed along beside him. Before long they reached a mountain, where the Bull King vanished without a trace. The Great Sage resumed his true form and entered the mountain to search. Within the mountain lay a deep pool of clear water. Beside it stood a stone tablet engraved with six large characters: “Emerald-Wave Pool, Tumbled-Rock Mountain.” The Great Sage thought, “That old bull has certainly gone beneath the water. The spirits below must be either flood-dragon spirits, dragon spirits, fish spirits, or perhaps spirits of tortoises, soft-shelled turtles, giant turtles, or alligators. Let old Sun go down and have a look.”

This is what he saw:

p.src: Hearing this, all the spirits at the feast rose, bowed to the old dragon, and said, “Sir Crab has only just entered your jade palace and does not know the king's etiquette. We beg Your Excellency to spare him and let him go.” The old dragon thanked them. The spirits then ordered, “Release that fellow. Let him remember this beating, and have him wait outside.” The Great Sage answered and fled for his life, going straight beneath the ornamental archway. He thought to himself, “The Bull King is here indulging in wine. How long would I have to wait for the feast to end? Even after it ends, he still will not lend me the fan. Better to steal his Golden-Eyed Beast, change into the Bull Demon King, and go deceive Princess Rakshasi. I shall trick her out of the fan and use it to send my master safely across the mountain. That would be the best plan.”

p.src: The Great Sage promptly resumed his true form, untied the Golden-Eyed Beast's reins, sprang up, mounted the carved saddle, and rode straight out from beneath the water. Once beyond the pool, he transformed himself into the likeness of the Bull King. Urging on the beast and riding the clouds, before long he reached the mouth of Plantain Cave on Mount Emerald Cloud. He called, “Open the door.” Two maidservants within the cave heard his voice and opened the door. Seeing the face of the Bull Demon King, they went in at once to report, “Mistress, Master has come home.” Hearing this, Rakshasi hurriedly arranged her cloudlike coiffure and hastened with lotus steps to the door to welcome him. The Great Sage dismounted from the carved saddle and led the Golden-Eyed Beast inside; boldly he set about deceiving the lovely lady. With only mortal eyes, Rakshasi failed to recognize him. She took him by the hand and led him inside, ordering the maids to set out seats and serve tea. Everyone in the household took him for their lord and treated him with the utmost respect and care.

p.src: After they had exchanged greetings, the “Bull King” said, “My lady, it has been long since we parted.” Rakshasi said, “May Your Majesty enjoy every blessing.” Then she added, “Your Majesty has been doting upon your new bride and has cast me aside. What wind has blown you here today?” The Great Sage laughed. “I would not dare cast you aside. Since Princess Jade-Face took me as her husband, household affairs have been burdensome and many friends have required my attention. That is why I have tarried away, though I have thereby established another household.” He continued, “I recently heard that the scoundrel Wukong, while escorting the Tang Monk, is drawing near the region of the Mountain of Flames. I fear he may come to borrow your fan. My hatred for him over the injury he did our son remains unavenged. If he comes, send someone to inform me. I shall seize him and tear his body into ten thousand pieces, to avenge the hatred we husband and wife bear him.” At these words Rakshasi shed tears and said, “Your Majesty, as the old saying goes, ‘A man without a wife has no mistress for his wealth; a woman without a husband has no master of her person.’ That macaque very nearly took my life.” Hearing this, the Great Sage deliberately flew into a rage and cursed, “When did that vile monkey pass through here?” Rakshasi replied, “He has not yet gone. Yesterday he came here to borrow the fan. Because he had harmed our child, I put on my armor, brandished my precious sword, and went out to cut down the macaque. He bore the pain, called me sister-in-law, and said that Your Majesty had once sworn brotherhood with him.” The Great Sage said, “Five hundred years ago, we did indeed swear brotherhood as seven brothers.” Rakshasi said, “When I cursed him, he dared not answer back; when I struck at him, he dared not fight. Afterward I swept him away with one stroke of my fan. I do not know where he found some art for anchoring himself against the wind, but early this morning he came shouting outside my door again. I used the fan again, but could not move him in the least. When I hastily swung my sword at him, he no longer held back. Fearing the weight of his cudgel, I fled into the cave and shut the door tight. I do not know how he did it, but he got inside my belly and nearly killed me. Only after I called him dear brother-in-law several times did I give him the fan and send him away.”

p.src: The Great Sage again feigned distress and beat his breast. “What a pity! What a pity! My lady, you made a mistake. How could you give that treasure to the macaque? It infuriates me!” Rakshasi laughed. “Your Majesty, calm your anger. The fan I gave him was a false one, merely to fool him into leaving.” The Great Sage asked, “Where is the true fan?” Rakshasi replied, “Do not worry, do not worry. I have it safely put away.” She ordered the maids to prepare wine, to welcome him home and celebrate. Then she raised a cup and offered it to him, saying, “Your Majesty, though you delight in your newly wedded bliss, you must never forget the wife who first bound up her hair with yours. For now, drink a cup of water from your old home.” The Great Sage dared not refuse. Smiling, he took the cup in his hand and said, “My lady, you drink first. In seeking to manage my property elsewhere, I have long been parted from you, while day and night you have guarded our home. Let this serve as a small token of my thanks.” Rakshasi took the cup back, filled it, and handed it to the king, saying, “From ancient times it has been said, ‘A wife is her husband's equal.’ A husband is the father who sustains his wife's very life. What need is there for thanks?” Only after the two had exchanged such courtesies did they sit down and begin passing the wine. The Great Sage dared not break his abstinence from meat and wine, so he ate only a few fruits while chatting with her.

She began pressing and rubbing against the Great Sage Sun, teasing and fondling him: taking his hand, she murmured tender endearments; leaning shoulder to shoulder, she bent close and whispered. From a single cup, first one took a sip, then the other, and they even fed each other fruit. The Great Sage answered false affection with feigned tenderness, keeping her company and smiling with her; helpless to do otherwise, he too nestled and leaned against her. Truly it was a case of:

p.src: Seeing her so thoroughly intoxicated, the Great Sage secretly grew vigilant and teased out the subject: “My lady, where have you put the true fan? You must guard it carefully at all times. Sun the Pilgrim has countless transformations; I fear he may return and trick you out of it.” Smiling merrily, Rakshasi spat it out from her mouth. It was no larger than an apricot leaf. Handing it to the Great Sage, she said, “Is this not the treasure?” The Great Sage took it in his hand but still doubted it, thinking to himself, “How could such a tiny thing fan out the flames? I fear this too may be false.” Seeing him stare thoughtfully at the treasure, Rakshasi could not restrain herself. She stepped forward, pressed her powdered cheek against the Pilgrim's face, and cried, “My darling, put the treasure away and drink. Why do you keep staring into space? What are you thinking about?” The Great Sage seized the opportunity and asked, “How can such a tiny object fan out eight hundred li of flame?” Wine had revealed Rakshasi's true nature, and without the least caution she explained the method: “Your Majesty, we have been parted for two years. I suppose you have been indulging in pleasure night and day, and Princess Jade-Face has addled your wits. How could you even forget the workings of your own treasure? Simply pinch the seventh strand of red silk on the handle with your left thumb and recite ‘𠲛噓啊吸嘻吹呼.’ It will immediately grow to a length of twelve feet. The transformations of this treasure are limitless! Even if the flames stretched eighty thousand li, a single sweep would extinguish them.”

p.src: Hearing this, the Great Sage firmly committed every detail to memory. He then held the fan in his mouth, wiped his face once, and revealed his true form. In a fierce voice he shouted, “Rakshasi, look closely! Am I truly your dear husband? You have pestered me with so much disgraceful behavior. Shame on you! Shame on you!” When the woman saw that he was Sun the Pilgrim, she panicked, overturned the table and banquet, and tumbled to the ground. Overwhelmed with shame and rage, she could only cry, “I am furious! I am furious!”

p.src: Indifferent to whether she lived or died, the Great Sage tore his hand free, strode away, and went straight out of Plantain Cave. Indeed: With no heart to covet beauty, he returned triumphant with a smiling face. With one bound he mounted an auspicious cloud and leapt up to a high mountain. There he spat out the fan and tried the method. With his left thumb he pinched the seventh strand of red silk on the handle and recited “𠲛噓啊吸嘻吹呼.” Sure enough, it grew to a length of about twelve feet. Holding it in his hand, he examined it again and again. It was indeed unlike the false one from before. Auspicious light shimmered upon it and blessed vapors swirled around it. Thirty-six strands of red silk ran warp and weft across its surface, linking the inside and outside together. It turned out that the Pilgrim had asked only for the method of making it grow, but had never asked for the spell to shrink it; no matter what he tried, it remained that same length. Having no other choice, he hoisted it onto his shoulder and returned by the old road. Of this we speak no more.

p.src: Now the Bull Demon King, having ended the banquet with the spirits at the bottom of the Emerald-Wave Pool, came out through the gate and found his Golden-Eyed Water-Repelling Beast gone. The old Dragon King gathered the spirits and asked, “Who let Lord Bull’s Golden-Eyed Beast loose and stole it?” The spirits knelt and said, “No one would dare steal it. We were all before the banquet, serving wine and carrying dishes, singing and playing music; not one of us was out here.” The old dragon said, “Our own entertainers would certainly not dare do such a thing. Did any stranger come in?” The dragon princes and their sons replied, “Just as everyone was taking their seats, a crab spirit came here. He was the only stranger.” On hearing this, the Bull King suddenly understood and said, “There is no need to say any more. This morning, when my worthy friend sent someone to invite me, Sun Wukong, who is escorting the Tang monk to fetch the scriptures, had found his way barred by the Mountain of Flames and came to ask me for the Plantain Fan. I refused, and he fought a bout with me, but neither of us prevailed. I then left him behind and came straight to the feast. That monkey is endlessly cunning and full of schemes. He must have transformed himself into the crab spirit, come here to spy out the situation, stolen my beast, and gone to deceive my wife into handing over the Plantain Fan.” At these words, every one of the spirits trembled with fear and asked, “Do you mean Sun Wukong, the one who caused havoc in Heaven?” The Bull King said, “The very one. Gentlemen, if you should encounter any trouble with him on the road to the Western Heaven, be sure to keep well out of his way.” The old dragon said, “If that is so, Great King, what will you do about your fine mount?” The Bull King laughed. “No matter, no matter. Gentlemen, you may all disperse while I go after him.”

p.src: With that, he parted the waters, leapt up from the bottom of the pool, mounted a yellow cloud, and went straight to the Plantain Cave on Emerald-Cloud Mountain. There he heard the Rakshasa Woman stamping her feet, beating her breast, and crying out at the top of her voice. He pushed open the door and saw the Golden-Eyed Water-Repelling Beast tethered below. The Bull King called loudly, “Wife, which way did Sun Wukong go?” When the maidens saw the Bull Demon, they all knelt and said, “Master, you have returned?” The Rakshasa Woman seized the Bull King and, knocking her head against him in anguish, cursed, “You wretched, heaven-doomed old fool! How could you be so careless as to let that macaque steal the Golden-Eyed Beast, assume your appearance, and come here to deceive me?” Grinding his teeth, the Bull King asked, “Which way did that macaque go?” Beating her breast, the Rakshasa Woman cursed, “That vile monkey tricked me out of my treasure, revealed his true form, and fled. I could die of rage!” The Bull King said, “Take care of yourself, wife, and do not fret. I shall catch up with that macaque, take back the treasure, flay his hide, smash his bones to pieces, and lay out his heart and liver to vent your anger.” Then he called, “Bring me a weapon!” A maiden replied, “Master, your weapon is not here.” The Bull King said, “Then bring me your mistress’s weapons.” The maidservants brought out two fine blue-steel swords. The Bull King took off the dark-green velvet jacket he had worn to the feast, tightened the close-fitting garments beneath it, seized a sword in each hand, strode out of the Plantain Cave, and rushed straight toward the Mountain of Flames in pursuit. Truly it was a case of this:
